Day, wide, bird’s-eye slightly dutch: an empty packed-earth Goguryeo farmyard, a stone well-rim, one thin dog, a timber grain-door standing open on nothing. A Western captain as a dark silhouette plants a dull gold-and-black banner in the dust at the centre. The south road is a pale stripe leaving the frame. High-key paper-white sky, yellow dust blooming at one edge. Device: the planted flag as the only vertical in a vacant yard. No faces. No granary. No army. PLACE: a nameless Goguryeo hamlet on the road south, timber posts, packed earth, a well — never a fortress slab. PAINTED STILL — no faces and no recognisable person: the only figure is one anonymous dark silhouette, a shadow-shape against the light that belongs to the place; the place or object IS the subject. Sensual and suggestive by shape and motion alone, never anatomical, never explicit. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). Hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL: granulated wet-in-wet washes and broken-colour dabs for sky, water and stone, dry-brush texture, soft bleeding edges and a faint paper grain; oil glazes deepen the darks and a touch of impasto lands on the single brightest highlight. Romantic-painting layout: one bold shape, at least half the frame quiet negative space, distant detail dissolving into haze. Film tenebrism: one hard directional key (sun, moon or lamp) against big dark masses, a thin edge of real light along the subject, painted bokeh from small real lights. Beautiful, luminous, painterly. NOT photoreal, NOT 3D, NOT a cartoon. No text. No watermark. DAY GROUND: the frame is built on WHITE — a high-key, paper-white ground: pale bright sky, white haze and mist, sunlit plaster and pale stone dissolving into bare white paper at the edges, the shadows few, crisp and cool-grey; the figure is the dark, inked thing in a bright frame. Never a black void, never a dim dusk wash.
